seo.title: MongoDB client for {devices}
seo.description: Query MongoDB in a mongosh-style JavaScript shell, edit documents as Extended JSON, rename fields across a collection, and connect to Atlas over SRV.

header.title: MongoDB client
header.lead: Query MongoDB with mongosh-style JavaScript, browse collections and edit documents as Extended JSON.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter a host or a replica-set host:port list, or paste a mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// URL. Sign in with SCRAM-SHA-1, SCRAM-SHA-256, X.509 or AWS IAM, with Auth Database set to the database that defines your user.

A host ending in .mongodb.net turns on SRV and TLS, which MongoDB Atlas requires; add your IP address to the cluster’s access list first, or the connection times out. New connections start with TLS off, and Preferred behaves as Required. Read Preference and Write Concern are set per connection.
notes: Through an SSH tunnel only the first host in the list is used, so replica set discovery and failover are off for that session.

bands.title: Query and edit documents
text: The Query tab takes mongosh-style JavaScript, with regex, ISODate(), variables, loops and forEach, and no shell to install. Top-level fields show as columns and nested objects as Extended JSON; cell edits keep dates and ObjectIds, and a nested edit updates only its path, such as address.city.

Insert Document and Edit Document use Extended JSON, and Edit Document refuses to save if the document changed while it was open. The filter bar reaches into nested objects and arrays, and Safe Mode counts a call as a read only when it only reads, such as find or an aggregate without $out or $merge.

bands.title: Collections, indexes and validators
text: The Structure tab lists indexes with their options, and Show DDL writes them as createIndex calls. Rename or remove a field across a collection with a previewed updateMany that updates the validator too, and New Table turns fields into a $jsonSchema validator.

<backup>Backup Dump</backup> writes the databases you tick, or single collections, to gzipped archives with {dumpTool}, and Restore Dump runs mongorestore into the database you pick. Install the MongoDB Database Tools first.

moveData: Import {importFormats} files into a collection, and export collections or results as {exportFormats}. An MQL export writes insertMany calls that run in mongosh, but a typed value nested in an array or subdocument becomes a string, so back those collections up with mongodump.

faq.question: Is the query tab mongosh?
faq.answer: No. It is a shell that accepts mongosh syntax and runs inside TablePro on JavaScriptCore, so most mongosh code runs as written. A whole number outside the 32-bit range is stored as a 64-bit integer, where mongosh stores a double: wrap it in Double() to match.

faq.question: How do I see a query plan?
faq.answer: Chain .explain("executionStats") onto the cursor in the query tab. The plan comes back as a document; MongoDB connections have no plan diagram.

faq.question: How do I list database users?
faq.answer: Run db.runCommand({usersInfo: 1}). The shell does not parse db.getUsers() or db.createUser().

otherTools.text: MongoDB Compass has visual aggregation pipelines, sampled schema analysis and explain plans, while TablePro queries MongoDB alongside other engines; see <compass>TablePro vs MongoDB Compass</compass>.
